editorial:
The Wolfpack is back for one last ride, and this time there is no wedding or bachelor party to blame for the chaos. Instead, a dangerous crime boss forces Phil, Stu, and Alan to track down the slippery Mr. Chow, turning their road trip into a wild heist across Tijuana and Las Vegas. The vibe is darker and more action-heavy than the first two films, but the heart of the series, the messy friendship between these guys, still carries the story.

Zach Galifianakis steals every scene as Alan, and Ken Jeong goes all out as the unpredictable Chow. The Las Vegas finale delivers some solid laughs and a fun sense of closure, though the jokes are fewer than in the original and the tone can feel heavy. If you are a fan of the trilogy, this is a decent send-off worth your time. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: The Wolfpack tracks Chow to Las Vegas, recovers the stolen gold, and hands it over to Marshall. But Marshall plans to kill them anyway. Chow shows up and shoots Marshall's henchmen, letting the guys escape with Doug safe. In a post-credits scene, Alan marries Cassie after another wild night, mirroring the first film's ending and hinting the chaos never really stops.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves buddy comedies and the Hangover trilogy.
